newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate steady, baht eases at close.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate steady, baht eases at close.

text.p: High liquidity in late Friday trade kept the Thai overnight interbank rate near its morning level of 7.00-7.25 percent against 7.00-8.00 late on Thursday, dealers said.

"An earlier expectation that a firmer dollar would trigger new active buying of the greenback did not materialise after the dollar fell sharply against major currencies in the afternoon. This may leave many people with long baht positions," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Some dealers said fast declining interbank rates this week could make the money market volatile when they rebound.

Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond on Tuesday repeated a call for local banks to cut interest rates to help boost the sagging economy. Several major local banks have responded by announcing cuts of prime lending rates.

The bid/offer range of the one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 8.00/8.50 satangs per dollar on late Friday, up from 7.50-8.50 in the morning and 7.00/7.50 late on Thursday. Most of the deals were made at 8.00-8.25, dealer said.
The central bank fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.51 against 25.49 on Thursday.
